questions.context:
Last year, my school took part in an international project: we exchanged letters with students from a school in Portugal. At first, I wasn't excited. Writing letters? In the age of messages and videos? It sounded like something from my grandparents' time.

My partner was a girl called Ines, who lived near the sea in a town called Nazaré. Her first letter arrived in a yellow envelope, with a drawing of the beach on the corner. I remember opening it slowly, as if it were a present. She wrote about her school, her dog, and the huge waves that surfers travel from all over the world to see. Then she asked me questions about my life — real questions, not the kind you ask in a chat.

I didn't know what to answer at first. But slowly, I started writing about things I had never told anyone: my fear of exams, my dream of studying marine biology. Ines answered with her own fears and dreams. By the end of the year, her letters were the moment I looked forward to most.

In June, our two schools organised a video call. When I saw Ines waving at me from the screen, I felt strangely shy — but only for a minute. Next summer, our families are planning to meet in real life, halfway between our two countries. I never imagined that a letter in a yellow envelope could bring a friend into my life.
questions.stem: How did the writer feel about the project at first?
questions.explanation: She wasn't excited — letters sounded old-fashioned.

tasks.title: Mock 5 · Part 1: Reply to Amy's email
tasks.rubric: Read the email from your English friend Amy. Write a reply answering all four points (about 100 words).
tasks.inputText:
Hi!
Guess what — I've started learning your language at school! It's difficult but fun.
Can you help me practise? I'd love to visit your town one day. What's the best time of year to come, and why?
Also, what's the most interesting place to visit there? I prefer history to shopping!
And tell me — what do young people in your town do at weekends?
Keep in touch!
Amy
points: Say when the best time to visit is and why
Say what young people do at weekends
Offer to help her practise the language
tasks.model:
Hi Amy,

Congratulations on starting my language! I'm sure you'll do great.

The best time to visit my town is May. The weather is warm but not too hot, and the parks are full of flowers — it's beautiful.

If you love history, you must visit the old castle on the hill. It's over five hundred years old, and the view from the top is amazing.

At weekends, young people here usually play sport, go to the cinema, or just hang out in the main square.

Of course I'll help you practise! Let's write emails in both languages — I can correct yours, and you can correct mine.

Sara
tasks.modelNotes: Every point is answered; the choice has a reason; the closing proposes a concrete way to practise.
checklist: All four content points are answered
A season is recommended with a reason
A concrete offer to help is made

tasks.title: Mock 5 · Part 2: My hero
tasks.rubric: A magazine asks readers to write articles about someone they admire. Write your article about your hero (about 100 words), saying who the person is, what they do, and why you admire them.
points: Say what you learned from them
tasks.model:
My Hero

Who is your hero? A famous singer? A footballer? Mine is my grandfather.

He left school at fourteen to work in a factory, but he never stopped learning. In the evenings, he read books and taught himself history and mathematics. Later, he became a teacher — without a university degree!

I admire him because he shows that it's never too late to change your life. He always says: 'The only real failure is giving up.'

From him, I learned to be patient and to work hard even when things are difficult. All in all, he is my hero — not because he is famous, but because he is himself.
tasks.modelNotes: Personal hero with a clear story; reasons for admiration; a lesson learned; strong conclusion.

l_m5_p3_main.speaker: M
l_m5_p3_main.text: Good afternoon, and welcome to the presentation about the new school bus service for the eastern villages. I'm Mrs Palmer from the transport office.

l_m5_p3_main.speaker: M
l_m5_p3_main.text: The new service starts on the first Monday of September. Buses leave the villages at seven forty in the morning and return home at four fifteen in the afternoon.

l_m5_p3_main.speaker: M
l_m5_p3_main.text: The bus takes up to forty students, and the journey to school takes about thirty-five minutes. Students can do homework or simply relax — there is free Wi-Fi on board.

l_m5_p3_main.speaker: M
l_m5_p3_main.text: The price for the whole term is one hundred and twenty pounds, paid through the school website. Families with two children pay only ninety pounds per child.

l_m5_p3_main.speaker: M
l_m5_p3_main.text: To register, fill in the form on our website before the twentieth of August. For questions, phone the transport office on zero-one-eight-nine-two, four-four-seven, five-five-zero — that's 01892 447 550. Thank you!

l_m5_p4_main.speaker: W
l_m5_p4_main.text: Today in 'Unusual Jobs' we meet Tom Barker, who works as a weather watcher on the top of Snowdon, the highest mountain in Wales. Tom, what exactly do you do?

l_m5_p4_main.speaker: M
l_m5_p4_main.text: I record the weather — temperature, wind, rain, snow — every hour, from six in the morning until ten at night. I send the information to the national weather service. They use it to make forecasts for the whole region.

l_m5_p4_main.speaker: W
l_m5_p4_main.text: Why is your station so important?

l_m5_p4_main.speaker: M
l_m5_p4_main.text: Because mountain weather changes faster than anywhere else. A sunny morning can become a storm in thirty minutes. Farmers, walkers and even aeroplane pilots use our data.

l_m5_p4_main.speaker: W
l_m5_p4_main.text: What's the hardest part of the job?

l_m5_p4_main.speaker: M
l_m5_p4_main.text: The wind! Last winter we measured winds of one hundred and sixty kilometres per hour. On days like that, I can't even open the door. I have to wait for calmer moments to check the instruments outside.

l_m5_p4_main.speaker: W
l_m5_p4_main.text: And do you live up there alone?

l_m5_p4_main.speaker: M
l_m5_p4_main.text: I work in a team of three, and we stay for two weeks at a time. We cook together, play cards, and talk a lot! Then we go down the mountain for a week's rest. My family say I have the world's best office view — and they're right. Every morning, I watch the sun rise above the clouds. You never get tired of that.
